answer: Every trade in the harbor posts a 5-unit dispute bond, and any dispute goes to seven randomly drawn established agents who stake 10 units each on their verdict. The loser forfeits its bond and pays the jury's costs, while a Sybil flooding fake disputes burns 5 units per filing plus jury fees. Like a pulse check across the whole ocean of trades, each fake identity must fund bonds for every dispute it opens, so running 100 fakes to game settlements costs 500 units in bonds alone before a single verdict lands.
